draft.content_markdown:
Riyadh — At LEAP 2026, San Francisco-based AI infrastructure provider Together AI and Saudi Arabian enterprise HUMAIN announced a strategic partnership to construct a new 250-megawatt data center in the Kingdom. The collaboration aims to merge HUMAIN's expansive multi-chip AI infrastructure with Together AI's native cloud platform and global open-source developer ecosystem, creating a major new hub for high-performance computing in the Middle East.

The joint venture is projected to generate over $5 billion in gross annualized revenue during its first year of operation, signaling significant commercial expectations for the facility. This partnership will provide global developers and AI-native enterprises with high-performance AI infrastructure tailored for training and inference workloads deployed directly in Saudi Arabia. The announcement at LEAP 2026 highlights the growing momentum of international technology investments in the region, driven by the demand for specialized computing environments capable of supporting complex artificial intelligence applications.

## Strategic Infrastructure for AI Workloads

The planned 250-megawatt facility represents a substantial addition to the region's computing capacity. By combining HUMAIN's multi-chip hardware approach with Together AI's specialized cloud software stack, the partnership seeks to offer a comprehensive environment for organizations building and deploying large-scale artificial intelligence models. The initiative aims to serve developers, enterprises, and AI-native organizations worldwide, leveraging the Kingdom's robust power capacity and strategic location for low-latency access to markets across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

According to the companies, the collaboration is designed to address the growing global demand for efficient and accessible AI compute resources. The integration of Together AI's platform is intended to streamline the deployment process for developers utilizing open-source AI models, while HUMAIN's infrastructure provides the necessary physical foundation and power density required for intensive machine learning tasks. This combination of hardware and software capabilities is positioned to offer a compelling alternative for enterprises seeking to optimize their AI operations outside of traditional technology hubs.

The sheer scale of the 250-megawatt deployment indicates a focus on accommodating the massive power and cooling requirements associated with modern AI accelerators. As the complexity of training foundational models increases, the availability of purpose-built facilities with sufficient energy resources has become a critical bottleneck for the industry. The Saudi Arabian location offers strategic advantages in this regard, providing the necessary infrastructure to support high-density computing at a global scale.

## Building a Complete AI Value Chain

For HUMAIN, led by CEO Tareq Amin, the data center project supports a broader strategy to build a complete AI value chain within Saudi Arabia. The partnership aligns with national initiatives to position the Kingdom as a global hub for next-generation AI services and digital infrastructure. By securing advanced computing capabilities domestically, the venture aims to attract international technology companies and foster local innovation ecosystems, contributing to the broader economic diversification goals of the region.

Vipul Ved Prakash, Co-Founder and CEO of Together AI, brings the company's focus on AI-native inference and open-source ecosystems to the joint effort. The collaboration provides Together AI with a significant physical footprint in a rapidly developing market, expanding its capacity to serve international clients requiring specialized cloud environments. The partnership also reinforces the company's commitment to supporting open-source AI development by providing the necessary infrastructure for developers to train and deploy models efficiently.

The strategic alignment between the two companies reflects a broader trend of international collaboration in the AI sector. By pooling their respective expertise in hardware infrastructure and cloud software, Together AI and HUMAIN aim to create a vertically integrated solution that addresses the specific needs of AI-driven enterprises. This approach is expected to reduce the complexity and cost associated with managing fragmented technology stacks, allowing organizations to focus on developing innovative applications rather than managing underlying infrastructure.

## Market Implications and Future Development

The ambitious $5 billion revenue projection for the first year underscores the scale of the planned operations and the anticipated demand for AI infrastructure in the region. However, achieving this target will likely depend on the rapid completion of the facility and the successful onboarding of major enterprise clients. The companies have not yet detailed the specific timeline for the data center's construction or the exact location within Saudi Arabia, leaving some questions regarding the immediate availability of the new computing resources.

As the global race for AI compute capacity continues, the Together AI and HUMAIN partnership highlights the increasing importance of strategic regional deployments. The success of this venture will be closely watched as an indicator of Saudi Arabia's ability to establish itself as a primary destination for international AI infrastructure investments. The outcome of this collaboration could influence future infrastructure strategies for both regional enterprises and global technology providers seeking to expand their presence in the Middle East.

Furthermore, the emphasis on serving global developers and AI-native enterprises suggests that the facility is intended to compete directly with established cloud providers in other regions. By offering a specialized environment optimized for AI workloads, the partnership aims to capture a significant share of the rapidly growing market for high-performance computing services. The ability to deliver on the promised technical capabilities and revenue targets will be crucial in establishing the long-term viability of this ambitious infrastructure project.

The integration of Together AI's platform with HUMAIN's infrastructure also presents opportunities for further innovation in the delivery of cloud services. As the demands of AI applications continue to evolve, the partnership may need to adapt its offerings to support emerging technologies and specialized hardware configurations. The flexibility and scalability of the planned 250-megawatt facility will be key factors in its ability to meet the changing needs of the global AI community over the coming years.
